samples.summary: The "binary-output command" parse-failure test asserts nothing binary-specific — it is a duplicate of the earlier missing-argument test
samples.evidence: `it('envelopes a missing argument on a binary-output command')` (test/output.test.ts:463-470) runs `docs export` and asserts exactly the same three things as the `docs content` test at :431 (code USAGE, same message, exitCode 1). It never checks that no bytes/partial file output reached stdout (no `stdoutSpy`/`writtenOut` assertion, unlike the :431 case), which is the only thing that would distinguish the binary-output path it claims to guard. As written it would pass identically for any command with a required first arg, so it adds no coverage beyond the earlier test.

samples.summary: No test appears to exercise the `commander.helpDisplayed` member of HELP_CODES
samples.evidence: HELP_CODES (src/cli.ts:41-45) lists three codes. The tests cover `--version` (commander.version), `--help` and bare `wafflebase` — in a given commander version those two produce only one of `commander.help` / `commander.helpDisplayed`, so one entry of the set is never exercised by any assertion. The suite asserts only observable stream/exit behaviour, never `e.code`, so a wrong or stale code string in the set would not be caught. Searched packages/cli/test for any reference to these codes (grep 'commander.help', 'helpDisplayed', 'CommanderError') — only comments in output.test.ts mention them.

samples.summary: No test covers subcommand-level `--help` / `--version`, where the inherited exitOverride is the load-bearing part
samples.evidence: root.ts:54 comments that `exitOverride` must be set before subcommands are registered because `.command()` copies the exit callback at creation time. The new tests only exercise help/version on the ROOT program (:475, :483, :491) and parse failures on children. Nothing asserts that e.g. `wafflebase docs --help` still prints help to stdout with exit 0 rather than being enveloped as a USAGE error, so a regression in the inherited help path for children would pass the suite. Searched the whole cli test dir for '--help' usages; only the three root cases exist.
searchedFor: grep for addCommand/new Command in packages/cli/src (only root.ts)

samples.evidence: The outer `beforeEach` (:347) sets `process.exitCode = 0` before every test, so the assertions at :480 and :488 hold unless something actively sets a non-zero code. They do add value only in combination with the stderr check; on their own they assert the fixture, not the behaviour. A stronger guard would set `process.exitCode` to a sentinel (e.g. 7) before the run and assert it is untouched/reset.

samples.summary: The `error: ` prefix strip is only tested for messages that carry the prefix
samples.evidence: cli.ts:87 applies `e.message.replace(/^error: /, '')`. Every new test feeds a commander message that starts with `error: `, so the anchored regex's behaviour on a CommanderError message WITHOUT the prefix (or one containing `error: ` mid-string) is unasserted. Low impact, but the strip is a silent message mutation with no negative case.
